correctness.rationale: For any synchronizing label string, different initial states force distinct modular effective-jump counts. This gives ≥n−1 b letters and ≥(n−2)(n−r) cyclic shifts; a missing-image induction shows the known word meets equality. Equality forces every b effective along an extremal trajectory, all a letters inside forced return intervals, and therefore uniquely fixes the word. Noncoprime residue obstruction, n=2 boundary and independent finite subset-BFS counts verified.

originality.rationale: Originality is confined to the exact singleton count of shortest reset-word labels for all coprime cyclic one-point-jump automata. Martyugin (2009) already states the threshold and an optimal word for the same class; those known parts are explicitly not novel. Its displayed claims do not assert or entail uniqueness. Full-text Don 2016 and Rystsov–Szykuła 2023 provide different reachability/upper-bound results. published-finding corpus related records do not imply the all-parameter singleton count. Other unindexed proofs remain possible.
residual_risks: A previous uniqueness proof under a different generator naming, one-cycle orientation or unpublished source may exist.
Some publisher or database records were not accessed in full; no independent novelty certification.
The previously known optimal length and constructed word must not be interpreted as new.

value.rationale: The exact optimizer multiplicity is a natural and previously unasserted structural invariant for the canonical cyclic/unitary family. A complete all-parameter singleton classification is stronger than the already-known threshold and example, is not implied by them, and provides a rigidity benchmark in contrast with families having exponentially many shortest reset words.
